title: The role of phosphoglycans in the susceptibility of Leishmania mexicana to the temporin family of anti-microbial peptides.
adjudication_summary: Worker-2/4/6 source re-review recovered Table 2 ED50 activity rows, reconciled linked DBAASP assay rows, preserved one database decimal conflict, and bounded mechanism claims to indirect phosphoglycan-susceptibility evidence.
summary: Source-reviewed worker-2/4/6 repair closed the complete-message rework ticket with cautions preserved; no blocking or major issue remains in the owned layers.

materials_exhausted.note: XML/PDF Table 2 and methods resolved activity; supplement is analytical mass/HPLC support and contains no additional activity/toxicity table; linked DBAASP rows were reconciled.

per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_1_database: DBAASP assay rows for Temporin F and Temporin L were checked against primary Table 1/2. Three linked value pairs match; the Temporin L amastigote 0.83 µM database value conflicts with primary 83 (46-93) µM and remains source_conflict.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_2_activity_toxicity: Primary XML/PDF Table 2 supports 20 ED50 rows for temporins A, B, 1Sa, F, and L across wild type promastigote, amastigote, Δlpg1, and Δlpg2 targets. No host-toxicity table is reported locally, so no toxicity rows were fabricated.
per_layer_decision_rationale.layer_3_mechanism: Mechanism claims are bounded to indirect mutant/surface-glycocalyx susceptibility context; no direct membrane or molecular-target mechanism is asserted.
per_layer_decision_rationale.worker_6_final_decision: Accepted with cautions after owned-layer repair because the remaining issues are conflict-preserving cautions, not blocking rework targets.

caution_findings.evidence_context: DBAASP linked assay/experiment rows report 0.83 µM for Temporin L amastigote ED50, while primary Table 2 reports 83 (46-93) µM. The database row remains source_conflict.

Table 2 and Results text support Temporin 1Sa amastigote ED50 as 42 (35-44) µM; a later conclusion sentence appears to cite 49 µM. The row-level artifact preserves the table value and records this as a nonblocking source inconsistency.
Local XML/PDF/supplement support parasite viability ED50 rows but do not report host-cell toxicity or hemolysis rows for this paper; no toxicity values were fabricated.
The paper supports surface glycocalyx/PPG susceptibility context by mutant phenotypes but does not run direct membrane binding, pore-formation, or permeability assays for the temporins in this study.
